questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Line ℓ is tangent to circle O at T. Prove that OT ⊥ ℓ. (Use an indirect argument.)
questions.prompt_markup: Line ℓ is tangent to circle O at T. Prove that OT ⊥ ℓ. (Use an indirect argument.)
questions.required_method: Suppose OT is not perpendicular; drop the perpendicular from O to ℓ at Q ≠ T; show a second point of ℓ is on the circle or inside it.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: if OQ ⊥ ℓ with Q ≠ T, then OQ < OT (the perpendicular is the shortest segment, as the hypotenuse OT is longest in right △OQT), so Q is inside the circle, and then ℓ would cross the circle twice, contradicting tangency. Invalid: "it looks perpendicular".

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: T lies on circle O, and P is outside it, with OT = 7, PT = 24 and OP = 26. Is line PT tangent to the circle at T? Justify your answer.
questions.prompt_markup: T lies on circle O, and P is outside it, with OT = 7, PT = 24 and OP = 26. Is line PT tangent to the circle at T? Justify your answer.
questions.correct_answer: No, PT is not tangent: 7² + 24² = 625 ≠ 676 = 26², so ∠OTP is not a right angle, and a tangent at T must be perpendicular to radius OT.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the computation, the conclusion "not tangent", and the reason (radius ⊥ tangent).

questions.prompt: T is on circle O with radius 6. Line ℓ is perpendicular to OT at T, and Q is a point on ℓ with TQ = 8. Find OQ, and explain why Q is outside the circle. What does this show about line ℓ?
questions.prompt_markup: T is on circle O with radius 6. Line ℓ is perpendicular to OT at T, and Q is a point on ℓ with TQ = 8. Find OQ, and explain why Q is outside the circle. What does this show about line ℓ?
questions.correct_answer: OQ = 10 > 6, so Q is outside. Every point of ℓ other than T is the end of a hypotenuse longer than OT, so ℓ meets the circle only at T: ℓ is tangent.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the length, the comparison, and the tangent conclusion.
